title: How many of you guys have finished and published a game on Steam?
author: BusinessZestyclose86
selftext:
How much do you generate a month from it? Is it worth paying the $100, or too over saturated? 

Did you have human testers before you launched it?

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: I released a game last year. A year later, I’ve sold about 130 copies; I haven’t even recouped the $100 I spent. Was it worth it? Only for the sake of what I learned.

replies.author: IrritableBrain
replies.body: Is your price for the game $1?

replies.author: thvaz
replies.body:
It was $10, but there were sales, returns, and so on. You have to hit $1000 to get the fee back, not $100. 

https://preview.redd.it/gukdh529vxvh1.png?width=845&format=png&auto=webp&s=844da2492beee5dbe2341123c0cae98e231d6f31

replies.author: TartNo3610
replies.body:
So you made $572 in profit? Wouldn’t that be considered recouping the $100 you spent? 

Genuinely asking.

replies.author: thvaz
replies.body: The $100 I spent to publish the game on Steam - the Steam fee. You have to earn $1000 to recoup it. Also this $572 is before the steam cut - what I earned in fact was about $300.

replies.author: IrritableBrain
replies.body: That's still earning money

replies.author: thvaz
replies.body: For 8 months of work? Not nearly enough.

replies.author: secter
replies.body:
But you’ve made your $100 fee back, and then $200 on top of that. It’s incorrect to say that you “haven’t even recouped the $100 \[you\] spent.”

I get that you feel the amount you’ve profited from selling on one platform alone in one year isn’t enough, but you’re not making sense.

It’s a no brainer to invest $100 once for something that returns $300 in the first year alone, which then just keeps generating profit.

replies.author: thatguywithimpact
replies.body:
$50/h 20 hours a week. You got $50k a year.

Then you go home and make games for those same 20h/week. You got $500.

You made about 50 cents/hour.

You can go on and say that 50 cent an hour might turn into a dollar or 2 in a few years. Maybe or maybe not. 

Now of course trying is better than not trying and making something creative is better than drinking beer and watching football. But let me real here, that ain't earning money

replies.author: BusinessZestyclose86
replies.body: They’re referring to the fact that after you make $1000 in revenue, Steam sends you the $100 you initially spent back. They don’t literally mean they haven’t seen a return.

comments.author: ChromaGolem
comments.body:
We released Alchemy Survivors back in April and it wasn't really meant to be a profit machine (we're still just exploring what kinds of AI mechanics are *fun* in games, so player feedback is *way* more valuable), but it has sold over 400 copies and recouped its $100 cost several times over.

The experience of publishing a game on Steam at least once is worth the $100 on its own IMO (if you really care for the game, and are excited to share it). You may or may not recoup it, but it's almost certainly worth it either way.

Alchemy Survivors, for reference: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4489800/Alchemy\_Survivors/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4489800/Alchemy_Survivors/)

We also have two more-ambitious demos launching in Next Fest next week (a farming sim where you create items in the game by drawing pixel art, and a company-building autobattler). Very excited to see how those fare; still a long way to see whether they'll make their $100 back, but they will at least be finished and published!

Fieldmade: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5110980/Fieldmade/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5110980/Fieldmade/)

Ultracapitalism: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5176610/Ultracapitalism/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5176610/Ultracapitalism/)

comments.author: TheSARMS_Coach
comments.body: Steam has over 140 million monthly active users. So no, it's not oversaturated. In most cases you will need to do some marketing and promo people actually know your game exists. Absolutely use Human testers. It's not hard to find a bunch of them here on Reddit. Plenty willing to support. So to answer your question about if it's worth the $100. If you think you have a decent game, for sure it is, but put in the work time, effort (and some money for promo) to actually sell the game, like you would do with any other product. People can't buy, what they don't know.
